newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on CBOT soycomplex fall.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on CBOT soycomplex fall.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended lower, pulled down in sympathy with a selloff in the CBOT soycomplex, traders said.
"The soyoil pressured us at the close. Louis Dreyfus was a big seller of the July," a trader said.

July WCE futures crush margin fell to -2.09 Tuesday from +0.34 Monday. About 1,000 July-Nov spread at $30, 860 July-Aug from C$1.20 to C$0.50 and Sep-Nov at $4. Volume was 5,350 lots, or 107,000 tonnes.
Japan bought 13,000-15,000 tonnes canola overnight, sources said.

July canola futures ended steady at $402.10 and November was down $3.20 at $371.70. July flax fell $2 to $331 but September rose $0.30 to $324 on commercial trade. Fifty Sep-Nov spread $2, traders said.

July western barley sank $3 to the contract low of $132.10 as Alberta Wheat Pool sold, October fell $1.50 to $133.80, 200 July-Oct spread at $0.50 with AWP a featured seller. Volume was 1,500. Oats did not trade.
July feed wheat closed $0.60 lower at $158.50 as UGG and Midland Walwyn bought. Commercials sold 200 December down $1.10 to $159 at the close, traders said.
PCTS sold 10 October feed pea contracts down US$0.50 to US$185.50 to a commercial, a trader said.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
